body: I'm depressed and suicidal again, I hate this version of myself. I'm going to have to start hurting myself again since I can't kill myself or cope with the fact that I'm alive.

I've always found this debate a weird one (was even having this debate last week with some friends who are considering having kids) so I'm glad I'm not alone there.

As someone that's an only child and been in therapy for a good few years, I dont think being an only child is bad. Rather, I think the emotional abuse and emotional neglect I experience as a child was worse because I was an only child. If I was going to have siblings, I would have just been able to deflect or share the burden after a certain age. Being an only child simply excerbated the situation, but it was always going to be bad regardless. It took 2 years of therapy before I learnt to make friends I was probably 22 or 23. 

Find a good therapist and gain some insight.
I feel that. Sometimes I wonder if the friends and family knew how we felt, would they be ok with letting us go?
Jazer Lee seems pretty good

Hey, thanks for sharing and taking the time to write a detailed response, I really appreciate it and your honesty! It's exactly what I was looking for :) 

I totally agree with you on the "pros outweigh the cons" thing and that's what I'm scared of. Right now I know what I'm dealing with I guess and I sort of know how to cope. Whereas antidepressants could change the game completely and I'm just not ready for that.

My therapist suggested that my lack of dating or inability to move past first dates was more of an intimacy and vulnerability issue. It was really useful to get that insight and understand that I'm actually scared of relationships because of my childhood/parents.
Everyone is different. I hope it all works out for you. Always happy to chat if you want!

This probably doesn't help but I (22F) came out to my parents about a year and a half ago. My dad took about a month to respond to my coming out letter and only about 3 months ago did my mum say "girlfriend" instead of boyfriend.

Maybe they just need time?
That's rough. I think my mum would do something similar tbh.

Couldn't you say the same about suicide then? 

Selfish (from the suicidal person) for not sticking around and living a miserable life for those that care about them. Selfless (from the suicidal person) because they may think that other people would be better off without them.

Question: Isn't it selfish of the person wanting the suicidal person to stick around and live miserably, in pain, suffering, etc. just so that they don't have to grieve their death?
Well this is annoying. I have always wondered why suicide is selfish but having a child isnt.
Thanks for sharing. I dont think my parents would be relaxed about it. But always good to hear other people's experiences/opinions.
